newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - July 31st 1997.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - July 31st 1997.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH -- BT TOLD TO OFFER CHEAP 'PHONES FOR ALL'

Telecoms industry watchdog Don Cruickshank has called for British Telecom to offer all UK homes the option of a new 'no frills', low-cost-telephone service, a decision that could cost BT up to 80 million stg per year. Oftel's 'Phones for All' programme, to be introduced next year, aims to ensure the estimated one million homes that would like to have a telephone, but are discouraged because of the price, will be able to afford the service. -- BSKYB FURIOUS AT REGULATOR'S DISNEY RULING

BSkyB has lashed out against an Independent Television Commission ruling that determined its customers should not be required to subscribe to two premium movie channels in order to receive the Disney Channel. The ITC continues to examine the issue of 'bundling', in which customers have to pay for groups of channels rather than just those they want to watch. Sky has reached a conclusion with Disney on its channel, the results of which will be presented to the ITC before the end of September. -- APPLE SET TO BRING BACK JOBS

It is believed Apple Computer will re-hire Alan Jobs next week, appointing the co-founder of the computer manufacturer as chairman. Jobs will reportedly take over some of the responsibilities of departed chairman and chief executive Gil Amelio, with the formal announcement expected to come at the Macworld Expo trade show in Boston. News of the rumoured appointment led to a $1-5/16 rise in Apple share prices on Wednesday to $17-11/16.
-- HINCHLIFFE AWARDED COSTS AFTER COURT REJECTS CLAIM

Vice chancellor Sir Richard Scott has awarded former Facia empire head Stephen Hinchliffe and his former business partner Christopher Harrison costs of up to 250,000 stg from retailer Sears. The costs were awarded following the rejection of an application by Facia Footwear's administrators, Price Waterhouse, that demanded the return of the 24.5m stg transferred from the shoe business before its collapse. -- LAURA ASHLEY AT NEW LOW AS THIRD DIRECTOR DEPARTS

Basha Cohen has resigned from her role as director of buying and design at retailer Laura Ashley to join US fashion house Tommy Hilfiger. Cohen is the third director in two months to leave Laura Ashley, and the announcement of her departure caused shares in the group to hit a new low of 50p and leaves many questioning the management style of chief executive Ann Iverson. -- NIGERIA SUMMONS SHELL AND MOBIL

Nigeria's government has made plans for an emergency summit in an attempt to solve a funding crisis in the oil industry caused by a 40 percent reduction in the industry's $3.3 billion budget, which is leading to a reduction in investment and is threatening future production. The government has summoned leading oil companies such as Shell and Mobil, who have lately been forced to cancel projects and lay off staff in the country due to the cutbacks.
THE GUARDIAN -- BECKETT ORDERS CLEAN-UP ON ELECTRICAL GOODS PRICES

The government has decided to abolish recommended retail prices on a range of consumer goods following a report from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission that said suppliers have retained high prices by refusing to sell to, or threatening to withdraw from, stores that discount goods. While the majority of consumer groups have approved the ruling, suppliers and dealers warn that once RRP's disappear, tight margins may lead to an increase in pricing. -- PEGGED DIVIDEND COSTS BAT DEAR

Tobacco and financial services concern BAT Industries has admitted it will not raise its half-year dividend, leading shares in the group to plummet 21p to 519p. BAT chief executive Martin Broughton said he expects the company to retain its full year dividend, though much of the company's future statements depend on whether or not President Bill Clinton approves BAT's compensation offer to smokers of 230 billion stg over the next 25 years. -- EMAP SELLS 13 TITLES

Emap, the publisher of magazines such as Press Gazette, Media Week and British Baker, has sold its line of magazines to Croydon-based Quantum Publishing in a reported 14 million stg deal. Quantum will pay 10 million stg in cash combined with a 4 million stg loan note. Emap's magazines have had total sales of about 14 million stg over the past year and employ 150 staff.
THE INDEPENDENT -- DISPLAY IT 'SEEMS TO HAVE DISAPPEARED'

On Wednesday, it emerged that troubled Internet software group Display IT had made no contact with its sole market-maker, JP Jenkins, since shares in the group were suspended two weeks ago. It has also been revealed that the phone numbers of Display IT and its founder, Peter Levin, have been disconnected. The Department of Trade and Industry has not confirmed whether or not an investigation into the company was ongoing, or if it was making any inquiry into the share suspension. -- ARNAULT QUESTIONS CALCULATIONS BEHIND GMG TAX CHARGE

In a further move to block the 23 million stg merger between Guinness and Grand Met, LVMH head Bernard Arnault has called for officials at both groups to disclose how they calculated the 1.5 billion tax bill that they believe will result from proposals to split the companies. Arnault will meet with institutional shareholders in Grand Met on Thursday in London to discuss his alternative proposals for a 15 billion stg wines and spirits group consisting of Moet Hennessy, IDV and United Distillers. -- DTI BACKS POWER COMPETITION TIMETABLE

The Department of Trades and Industry has urged the government and the electricity regulator to offer incentives to companies that adhere to the timetable for introducing domestic electricity competition in the UK. The government has indicated it will do all it can to ensure the process is not determined "by the speed of the slowest player".
